event: response.output_text.done
data: {"content_index":0,"item_id":"","logprobs":[],"output_index":0,"sequence_number":337,"text":"## Purpose\n\nA production HTTP gateway needs separate connection, first-byte, idle-stream, and total-request timeouts because each limits a different phase of work. The connection timeout bounds establishing an upstream connection, including applicable transport and TLS handshakes. The first-byte timeout bounds waiting for the upstream response to begin after sending the request. The idle-stream timeout limits gaps between response reads, while the total-request timeout caps the entire operation, including retries and streaming.\n\n## Failure modes\n\nWithout a connection timeout, unreachable hosts or stalled handshakes can consume sockets and concurrency slots. Without a first-byte timeout, an upstream that accepts connections but never responds can hold capacity indefinitely. Without an idle-stream timeout, a response can start successfully and then stop making progress. Without a total deadline, an upstream can send occasional bytes forever, continually resetting the idle timer.\n\nOne timeout cannot safely replace the others: a short universal limit breaks legitimate long streams, while a long limit permits expensive stalls during connection establishment or response startup. Progress-sensitive timers alone cannot bound overall resource consumption.\n\n## Operational guidance\n\nPropagate cancellation when any deadline expires or the client disconnects, stopping upstream work, pending retries, and related tasks where supported. Clean up connection-pool state explicitly: return connections only when protocol state is known to be reusable; otherwise close them or reset the affected multiplexed stream without disrupting unrelated requests.\n\nIf streaming headers or body bytes have already reached the client, the gateway generally cannot substitute a fresh error response. Terminate or reset the stream and record that the response was partial.\n\nChoose phase-specific limits from latency objectives and workload behavior, enforce an overall deadline, and monitor timeout causes separately.","type":"response.output_text.done"}
